subject: Pricing & batching follow-up: token volumes, budget, continuous batching
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 15:05:00 -0000
Subject: Pricing & batching follow-up: token volumes, budget, continuous batching

Thanks again for taking the time today, Alex — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we have aligned expectations: 

1) Current usage profile (what you described on the call)
- Peak QPS: ~40 concurrent requests (spiky, but sustained bursts for 3–5 minutes)
- Average request size: 1.2k tokens in, 350 tokens generated per request (summary / assistant responses)
- Typical pattern: sustained background traffic (streaming summary jobs) + interactive bursts from power users

2) Expected growth / target volumes
- Target production launch: 5–7M requests/month (pilot), steady-state target 30–50M requests/month in 12 months assuming product expansion
- Rough token estimate (baseline): ~12B input tokens + ~3.5B output tokens/month (~15.5B total) — see attached token-estimates.xlsx for line-item math

3) Pricing & budget guardrails (what you mentioned)
- Budget range: $6k–$18k/month initially for pilot, aiming to converge to enterprise commit later
- Target unit economics you asked about: target $/1M tokens in the range of $150–$300 (your procurement target was closer to $200/1M)

4) Batching & concurrency assumptions (continuous batching conversation)
- Workload: high percentage of steady-state background jobs that batch well (many similar prompts, predictable sequences) — this favors continuous batching and large prefix caching
- Concurrency model: we expect continuous batching to smooth the token cost by ~1.4–1.8x (token-efficiency multiplier) compared to naive single-request serving in your workload; exact factor depends on request-size distribution and acceptable tail latency
- Latency SLOs: interactive requests need 200–300ms p95; background jobs can tolerate higher latency and be batched aggressively

5) Next steps
- I will loop in SE to set up a 60-min technical session next week to validate batching gains and run a short perf pass on a sample corpus (provision a small eval) — proposed slots sent separately
- I'll attach a first-pass mutual action plan (MA-plan.xlsx) and the token estimates for you to review
- Marissa/Aditya: can you confirm preliminary target pricing bands for ACME given the volume profile above so Alex has a baseline for procurement?

Attachments: MA-plan.xlsx, token-estimates.xlsx, redwood-pricing-guide.pdf

Thanks — happy to adjust numbers if I misunderstood anything from the call.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pricing & batching follow-up: token volumes, budget, continuous batching

Thanks Alex — answers inline below and see attachments for an example perf run: 

1) Batching benefit: the 1.4–1.8x figure is an effective token-efficiency multiplier (i.e., fewer billed tokens per logical request) we often see on continuous-background workloads where requests share prefixes and models support KV caching. That maps to cost-per-1M-tokens equivalence: if native per-token cost is $250/1M, a 1.5x batching multiplier would yield an effective $167/1M on that workload class.

2) Latency tradeoff: interactive p95 constraints reduce batching headroom. In practice we throttle continuous batching so interactive traffic gets priority; for your 200–250ms p95 target we expect to keep most interactive requests unbatched or using very small micro-batches, while background jobs absorb larger batches. Net effect: you still realize a meaningful batching uplift (we estimate ~1.3x overall) with tailored routing policies. We'll validate in the SE call.

Security one-pager: attached redwood-pricing-guide.pdf includes a short SOC2 + residency excerpt; I will send a concise vendor one-pager separately (and loop security if needed).

Proposed SE session: Thu 2026-07-29 at 14:00 PT / 17:00 ET — does that work? If not, suggest two other slots and Marissa/Aditya will join to cover pricing tradeoffs.

Best,
Camila

Alex — looping on pricing. Quick baseline guidance given the profile Camila outlined: 

- Pilot (5–10M requests / month, ~1–3B total tokens): list-equivalent pricing guidance: $275/1M tokens
- Mid-stage (30–50M requests / month, ~10–20B tokens): committed band guidance: $160–$200/1M tokens depending on term and reserved capacity commit
- Continuous-batching uplift: we typically model a 1.2–1.6x effective token efficiency for workloads like yours (higher if prefix caching is strong) — pricing band above assumes we realize ~1.4x on long-run steady state

I'll prepare a short pricing sheet for the SE call that maps your token-estimates.xlsx to the three bands (pilot / mid / committed). Camila — I'll attach the pricing workbook to the SE invite and flag any approval notes needed from finance.

Marissa
